prompt: CHALLENGE: Phenoxide (PhO⁻) + CH₂=CH-CH₂-Br (allyl bromide) can react at O (SN2) OR at the ortho/para ring carbon (C-alkylation via enolate-like resonance). Which usually dominates in polar aprotic solvent, and why?

options.label: O-alkylation dominates in polar aprotic solvents like DMF or acetone — the hard-charged O is the site of highest HOMO coefficient; soft C sites favored only in protic solvents that cluster around O.

explanation: Phenoxide is ambident. In polar aprotic solvents (DMF, acetone), charge sits on O (highest HOMO there) → O-alkylation to allyl phenyl ether. In protic (H₂O, EtOH), O is H-bonded and softer C becomes the main site → C-alkylation. Allyl halides are 'softer' electrophiles and amplify this trend. Classic Hard/Soft Acid-Base (HSAB) problem.
